"""The rllab command: each trigger to its pipeline entry, the result printed (AD-10).

`cli` owns no pipeline step: it parses arguments, calls the entry, prints the returned contract
type and sets the exit code. Every error is printed as one line naming its cause, exit code 1.
"""

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence
from pathlib import Path

from rllab.cli.pipelines.pl04_watch import run_watch
from rllab.cli.pipelines.pl05_chart import run_chart
from rllab.cli.pipelines.pl06_evaluate import run_evaluate
from rllab.train.pipelines.pl01_check import run_check
from rllab.train.pipelines.pl03_batch import run_batch
from rllab.train.types import CheckResult


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run one `rllab` subcommand; 0 on success, 1 on an error or a failed method check."""
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:
        result = _dispatch(args)
    except Exception as exc:  # every error becomes one line and exit code 1 (cli.main contract)
        print(f"rllab {args.command}: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    items = result if isinstance(result, list) else [result]
    for item in items:
        print(item)
    failed = any(isinstance(item, CheckResult) and not item.passed for item in items)
    return 1 if failed else 0


def _dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
    """Call the entry of the parsed subcommand (`train` is a one-seed `batch`)."""
    match args.command:
        case "check":
            result: object = run_check(args.config, args.seed)
        case "train":
            result = run_batch(
                args.config, [args.seed], args.root, workers=1, check_seed=args.check_seed
            )
        case "batch":
            result = run_batch(
                args.config,
                args.seeds,
                args.root,
                workers=args.workers,
                check_seed=args.check_seed,
            )
        case "watch":
            result = run_watch(args.run_path)
        case "chart":
            result = run_chart(
                args.project,
                args.world,
                args.variant,
                include=args.include,
                measure=args.measure,
            )
        case _:  # "evaluate": argparse admits only the subcommands above
            result = run_evaluate(
                args.project,
                args.world,
                args.variant,
                include=args.include,
                workers=args.workers,
            )
    return result


def _seeds(text: str) -> list[int]:
    """Seeds as `1-5` (inclusive) or `1,3,5`."""
    try:
        if "-" in text:
            first, last = (int(part) for part in text.split("-", 1))
            return list(range(first, last + 1))
        return [int(part) for part in text.split(",")]
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"seeds must look like 1-5 or 1,3,5: {text!r}") from exc


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="rllab", description=__doc__)
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    check = commands.add_parser("check", help="run the method check of a config (PL-01)")
    check.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    check.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)

    train = commands.add_parser("train", help="train one seed of a config (PL-03, one seed)")
    train.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    train.add_argument("--seed", type=int, required=True)
    train.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    train.add_argument("--check-seed", type=int, default=0)

    batch = commands.add_parser("batch", help="train several seeds in parallel (PL-03)")
    batch.add_argument("config", type=Path)
    batch.add_argument("--seeds", type=_seeds, required=True)
    batch.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    batch.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=None)
    batch.add_argument("--check-seed", type=int, default=0)

    watch = commands.add_parser("watch", help="show a run's progress (PL-04)")
    watch.add_argument("run_path", type=Path)

    chart = commands.add_parser("chart", help="draw the learning curve (PL-05)")
    _add_world_args(chart)
    chart.add_argument("--measure", default=None)

    evaluate = commands.add_parser("evaluate", help="evaluate against both baselines (PL-06)")
    _add_world_args(evaluate)
    evaluate.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=None)
    return parser


def _add_world_args(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    parser.add_argument("world")
    parser.add_argument("variant")
    parser.add_argument("--include", action="append", default=[], metavar="NAME")
    parser.add_argument("--project", type=Path, default=Path())

The entries are replaced by recorders, so these tests hold whatever the entries become.

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from tests.contracts import decode, load

from rllab.cli import commands, main


@pytest.fixture
def calls(monkeypatch):
    """Each entry records its arguments and returns its fake's answer."""
    seen: list[tuple[str, tuple, dict]] = []
    answers = {
        "run_check": [decode.check_result(load.sample("train.CheckResult", "dqn_pass"))],
        "run_batch": [load.module("runlog.Run", "double").recorded_run().record],
        "run_watch": decode.progress(load.sample("runlog.Progress", "snake_35pct")),
        "run_chart": decode.output(load.sample("core.Output", "snake_curve")),
        "run_evaluate": [decode.summary(load.sample("evaluate.Summary", "snake_pass"))],
    }
    for name, answer in answers.items():

        def entry(*args, _name=name, _answer=answer, **kwargs):
            seen.append((_name, args, kwargs))
            return _answer

        monkeypatch.setattr(commands, name, entry)
    return seen


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("argv", "expected"),
    [
        (["check", "c.toml"], ("run_check", (Path("c.toml"), 0), {})),
        (
            ["train", "c.toml", "--seed", "3"],
            ("run_batch", (Path("c.toml"), [3], Path("runs")), {"workers": 1, "check_seed": 0}),
        ),
        (
            ["batch", "c.toml", "--seeds", "1-5", "--workers", "2"],
            ("run_batch", (Path("c.toml"), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], Path("runs")),
             {"workers": 2, "check_seed": 0}),
        ),
        (["watch", "runs/snake/default/a"], ("run_watch", (Path("runs/snake/default/a"),), {})),
        (
            ["chart", "snake", "default", "--include", "a", "--measure", "length"],
            ("run_chart", (Path(), "snake", "default"), {"include": ["a"], "measure": "length"}),
        ),
        (
            ["evaluate", "snake", "default", "--project", "p"],
            ("run_evaluate", (Path("p"), "snake", "default"), {"include": [], "workers": None}),
        ),
    ],
    ids=["check", "train", "batch", "watch", "chart", "evaluate"],
)  # fmt: skip
def test_each_trigger_calls_its_entry(calls, capsys, argv, expected):
    assert main(argv) == 0
    assert calls == [expected]
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip()

"""`rllab` dispatches each M1 trigger to its pipeline entry, prints the result, sets the exit code.

The entries are replaced by recorders, so these tests hold whatever the entries become.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from tests.contracts import decode, load

from rllab.cli import commands, main


@pytest.fixture
def calls(monkeypatch):
    """Each entry records its arguments and returns its fake's answer."""
    seen: list[tuple[str, tuple, dict]] = []
    answers = {
        "run_check": [decode.check_result(load.sample("train.CheckResult", "dqn_pass"))],
        "run_batch": [load.module("runlog.Run", "double").recorded_run().record],
        "run_watch": decode.progress(load.sample("runlog.Progress", "snake_35pct")),
        "run_chart": decode.output(load.sample("core.Output", "snake_curve")),
        "run_evaluate": [decode.summary(load.sample("evaluate.Summary", "snake_pass"))],
    }
    for name, answer in answers.items():

        def entry(*args, _name=name, _answer=answer, **kwargs):
            seen.append((_name, args, kwargs))
            return _answer

        monkeypatch.setattr(commands, name, entry)
    return seen


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("argv", "expected"),
    [
        (["check", "c.toml"], ("run_check", (Path("c.toml"), 0), {})),
        (
            ["train", "c.toml", "--seed", "3"],
            ("run_batch", (Path("c.toml"), [3], Path("runs")), {"workers": 1, "check_seed": 0}),
        ),
        (
            ["batch", "c.toml", "--seeds", "1-5", "--workers", "2"],
            ("run_batch", (Path("c.toml"), [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], Path("runs")),
             {"workers": 2, "check_seed": 0}),
        ),
        (["watch", "runs/snake/default/a"], ("run_watch", (Path("runs/snake/default/a"),), {})),
        (
            ["chart", "snake", "default", "--include", "a", "--measure", "length"],
            ("run_chart", (Path(), "snake", "default"), {"include": ["a"], "measure": "length"}),
        ),
        (
            ["evaluate", "snake", "default", "--project", "p"],
            ("run_evaluate", (Path("p"), "snake", "default"), {"include": [], "workers": None}),
        ),
    ],
    ids=["check", "train", "batch", "watch", "chart", "evaluate"],
)  # fmt: skip
def test_each_trigger_calls_its_entry(calls, capsys, argv, expected):
    assert main(argv) == 0
    assert calls == [expected]
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip()


def test_batch_takes_a_seed_list(calls):
    assert main(["batch", "c.toml", "--seeds", "1,3"]) == 0
    assert calls[0][1][1] == [1, 3]


def test_a_failed_method_check_exits_1(calls, monkeypatch, capsys):
    failed = decode.check_result(load.sample("train.CheckResult", "ppo_fail"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(commands, "run_check", lambda *args: [failed])
    assert main(["check", "c.toml"]) == 1
    assert "passed=False" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_an_error_is_one_line_naming_its_cause_and_exits_1(monkeypatch, capsys):
    def missing(*args, **kwargs):
        raise FileNotFoundError("no config file at c.toml")

    monkeypatch.setattr(commands, "run_check", missing)
    assert main(["check", "c.toml"]) == 1
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert err == "rllab check: FileNotFoundError: no config file at c.toml\n"

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as caught:
        main(["batch", "c.toml", "--seeds", "one-five"])

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook (becomes SubagentStop inside a subagent): block finishing until the gate passes.
#   stop_gate.sh collect|gate|full [--warn]
# Blocks by printing {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} and exiting 0, not by exit 2:
# Claude Code treats an exit-2 Stop hook whose stderr mentions a missing file
# ("No such file or directory") as non-blocking, and test output often does.
# Loop guard: after MAX_TRIES failed attempts the agent may stop. Outside a dt build the last
# block tells it to start its report with "GATE FAILED", because that report is all the parent
# sees: a SubagentStop systemMessage doesn't reach the main view (checked live, Claude Code 2.1.292).
# --warn never blocks: a failing gate only leaves a systemMessage (CONSTRAINTS.md says when).
# For gate and full, .claude/.check_pkg (written by dt claim, optional) holds the task's package
# and becomes --pkg.
# In a dt build, .claude/.dt (written by dt claim) holds the path to dt.py: an agent whose claim
# has an escalation record (dt escalate) may stop without the gate, and every gate result is
# recorded with `dt build verdict`, which dt land reuses when the tree hasn't changed since.
mode=gate
warn=0
for a in "$@"; do
  case "$a" in
    --warn) warn=1 ;;
    *) mode="$a" ;;
  esac
done
MAX_TRIES=3
source "$(dirname "$0")/project_root.sh"

# Without jq there is no safe way to write the JSON answer: block the plain way (exit 2,
# fixed message) rather than let the agent stop on a gate nobody ran.
say_block() {
  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    jq -n --arg reason "$1" '{decision: "block", reason: $reason}'
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "stop_gate: the gate failed and jq is not installed to report it; install jq, then run scripts/check.sh $mode" >&2
  exit 2
}
say_user() {
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && jq -n --arg msg "$1" '{systemMessage: $msg}'
  exit 0
}

cd "$root" || say_block "stop_gate: cannot enter the project root $root"
id=$(jq -r '.agent_id // .session_id // "main"' <<<"$input" 2>/dev/null | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9_-')
counter=".claude/.stop_attempts_${id:-main}"
mkdir -p .claude

dt=""
[ -s .claude/.dt ] && dt=$(head -n 1 .claude/.dt)
if [ -n "$dt" ] && python3 "$dt" build escalated >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rm -f "$counter"
  exit 0
fi

pkg_args=()
if [ "$mode" != collect ] && [ -s .claude/.check_pkg ]; then
  pkg_args=(--pkg "$(tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9_.-' <.claude/.check_pkg)")
fi

out=$(bash scripts/check.sh "$mode" ${pkg_args[@]+"${pkg_args[@]}"} 2>&1)
rc=$?
[ -n "$dt" ] && python3 "$dt" build verdict --mode "$mode" --rc "$rc" >/dev/null 2>&1
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  rm -f "$counter"
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$warn" = 1 ]; then
  say_user "Gate '$mode' is failing (warn only, not blocking). Run scripts/check.sh $mode to see why."
fi

tries=$(cat "$counter" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
[[ $tries =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || tries=0
tries=$((tries + 1))
echo "$tries" >"$counter"
if [ "$tries" -gt "$MAX_TRIES" ]; then
  rm -f "$counter"
  say_user "Gate '$mode' still failing after $MAX_TRIES attempts; the agent stopped so a human can look. Run scripts/check.sh $mode."
fi

last=""
if [ "$tries" -eq "$MAX_TRIES" ] && [ -n "$dt" ]; then
  last="
This was the last attempt. If you can't fix it now, finish anyway with your status line:
the failing verdict is recorded, and dt land rejects the task with it."
elif [ "$tries" -eq "$MAX_TRIES" ]; then
  last="
This was the last attempt. If you can't fix it now, finish anyway and start your report with
\"GATE FAILED: scripts/check.sh $mode\", then list what is still failing."
fi
say_block "Gate '$mode' failed (attempt $tries/$MAX_TRIES). Fix these before finishing:
$(echo "$out" | tail -60)$last"

                   {TEST-WRONG,CONTRACT-CHANGE,NEEDS-DEP} why

positional arguments:

                        express what the task needs (risk.Drawdown)
